source_text: non habiturum fuisse quid facerem, quo confugerem; cum tuis argumentationibus unde occurrerem reperire non possem me imbellem tibi opinionem consortis opponere, et velut consternatum metu, conscios nominare?
pass_a_gloss: Not habiturum to-have-been what facerem, whither confugerem; when/with tuis argumentationibus whence occurrerem reperire not possem me imbellem to-you opinionem consortis opponere, and as-if consternatum by-fear, conscios nominare?
pass_b_english: [If he were] pressed by the judges’ authority, [he would] have nothing to do and nowhere to turn, since he could find no answer to my arguments.
Opinions should be weighed, not counted.
A crowd of blind people is no help in discovering anything.
[He] sets against me the helpless opinion of an ally and, as though panic-stricken, names his accomplices.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
